newsitem.title: CHINA: China aims to improve financial supervision.
newsitem.headline: China aims to improve financial supervision.

text.p: China plans to improve supervision over its financial system this year by introducing rules that will help control risk, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The People's Bank of China, the central bank, plans to issue rules on required internal controls for financial institutions, the newspaper said, quoting the bank's recently published 1997 China Financial Outlook.
The rules would help financial institutions control risk, as well as allow the government to obtain accurate information about the activities of banks, the central bank report said.
The People's Bank would also issue a manual on financial supervision to its offices around China to define the functions of central bank departments, it said.
China would draw up methods to evalute the quality of bank assets, based on international accounting standards adapted to local Chinese conditions, the newspaper said.
The country would also speed up the establishment of a banking association, which would bring banks together to draft joint pledges and rules on fair competition, it said.
It did not say when the association would be established.
